issues.title: Partition distinct radix HT on group-key hash
issues.hypothesis: q16 is 100% of the workload and its HASH_GROUP_BY (count DISTINCT) takes 0.43s of operator time, more than the join (0.17s). DuckDB runs count(DISTINCT x) GROUP BY G in two levels. First a distinct radix HT on (G,x), then each distinct partition is scanned and re-sunk into the main HT on G. The distinct HT is partitioned on hash(G,x), so every distinct partition holds rows from nearly every group. The re-sink into the main HT (measured ~180ms CPU earlier) therefore builds many scattered groups per task, and those must be combined again. If the radix bits of the distinct hash come from hash(G) instead, each distinct partition holds whole groups. The main-HT re-aggregation then becomes partition-local and small. A prior run of this exact mechanism measured q16 193.5->167.9ms and 180.8->158.7ms (-12..-13%).
issues.plan: In RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink (src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:548), when the table is a distinct table (needs a flag set from PhysicalHashAggregate's ctor / DistinctAggregateData setup in src/execution/operator/aggregate/physical_hash_aggregate.cpp) with a non-empty group set: compute h_full = group_chunk.Hash() over all columns and h_g = hash over only the first |G| columns. Splice the bits in the radix-partition mask range (RadixPartitioning, MAX_RADIX_BITS bits, i.e. bits [36,48) in the current hash layout; verify in radix_partitioning.hpp) from h_g into h_full. Then call the GroupedAggregateHashTable::AddChunk(groups, group_hashes, payload, filter) overload (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:564) with those hashes, not the overload that hashes internally. The hash is stored in the row, so repartition and finalize stay consistent. Gate on estimated_cardinality >= 4096 and skip the TryAddCompressedGroups/dictionary fast path when enabled, because it hashes internally. Check that the main-HT sink in the distinct finalize (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp ~line 656-733) still gives correct results. Optionally give each finalize task a single distinct partition so its main-HT sink is local.
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY with count/sum(DISTINCT) and grouping keys, a common analytical shape. No effect on non-distinct aggregates. If there are very few groups (e.g. 1-10), partitions become skewed and parallelism drops. Hence the cardinality gate, plus a possible extra gate when the estimated group count is below the partition count.
issues.risk: Medium. Hash consistency must hold everywhere distinct rows are inserted or reinserted, including the dictionary/compressed paths and spill/external repartition. Skewed partitions when there are few groups. The idea was already validated once, so the main risk is implementation correctness.

issues.title: Skip unpartitioned staging for heap-layout agg HTs
issues.hypothesis: The join feeds the aggregate ~300-row chunks, so FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (aggregate_hashtable.cpp ~line 758) sends new groups to unpartitioned_data staging. Abandon/ClearPointerTable later repartitions them, which copies the VARCHAR heap and recomputes pointers. Measured earlier: Abandon 37->2ms and MaybeRepartition 97->56ms CPU when staging only for AllConstant layouts. Wall time was about -5% (noisy).
issues.plan: In GroupedAggregateHashTable::FindOrCreateGroupsInternal, use the unpartitioned staging path only when layout.AllConstant(); otherwise append directly to partitioned_data.
issues.generality: Aggregates with VARCHAR/nested keys fed by small chunks. Fixed-width layouts are unchanged.
issues.risk: Low. Two-line gate. Spill paths need a test with long-string keys.

dispatch: Partition distinct radix HT on group-key hash
output.memory:
# Memory

## Round g1r1 (2026-11-23)
- Workload: q16 only (count DISTINCT ps_suppkey GROUP BY p_brand,p_type,p_size; partsupp JOIN part, NOT IN supplier MARK join). Baseline 179ms.
- Profile: HASH_GROUP_BY 0.43s operator time (dominant), partsupp scan + inner HJ 0.17s, part side ~0.01s, supplier LIKE scan 0.02s.
- Facts from prior runs of db_evolve (global auto-memory, same engine):
  - Distinct HT partitioned on hash(G): q16 -12..-13%. Dispatched this round.
  - Skip unpartitioned staging for heap (VARCHAR) layouts: ~-5%, noisy. In backlog.
  - Early HT grow (-3%), early SkipLookups (<=3%): noise. Don't repeat.
  - Join output reaches agg as ~300-row chunks; main-HT re-sink ~150ns/row.
  - Gotcha: wrapping q16 in count(*) lets the optimizer drop DISTINCT; use max(cnt) instead.
- Code locations: RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:548; GroupedAggregateHashTable::AddChunk(groups, hashes, payload, filter) aggregate_hashtable.cpp:564; FindOrCreateGroupsInternal :641, staging at ~:758; distinct finalize in physical_hash_aggregate.cpp ~656-733.

## Next ideas if the dispatch lands
- Unpartitioned-staging gate (backlog).
- Join-side work: partsupp scan 0.17s with BF + min/max dynamic filters; try the probe side or a perfect HJ on dense part keys.
- Compact join output chunks before the agg sink.
